latest_release.name: 3proxy-1.0.3
latest_release.body:
Security fixes (RADIUS, reverse DNS authentication), stability and performance fixes, -s renamed to -B for SNI break

! Fix: RADIUS authentication: the reply digest copied the shared secret right after the received bytes, so a reply of 4100 bytes with a secret of 17 or more characters wrote up to 47 bytes of it past the reply buffer on the stack, before the reply was authenticated; the digest is hashed over the reply and the secret in place now, with nothing written past the reply, and a reply is taken only from the address and port of the server the request went to, with the request's identifier and length, which was never checked before
! Fix: the PTR answer of a name server could write past the answer buffer on the stack: the label walk ran to the end of the whole message instead of the end of the record's data and could take a compression pointer for a label length (an answer of 3841 bytes or more reached past the buffer itself); the walk now stops at the end of the record's data, and a compressed, empty or truncated name is not accepted
! Fix: every connection matching a pcre: (or regex:) rule matched on the one match data block of the rule, which pcre2_match() writes into: two connections matching at the same time raced and corrupted memory, bringing the process down under load; a connection now makes a match data block of its own
! Fix: TLS: a read which could only be done once a write was, or a write once a read was (a TLS 1.3 key update answered while the socket cannot take more, for example), ended the connection with an error; each TLS socket remembers now what its pending read and write wait for, and the poll of the TLS layer waits for that
! Fix: Windows: a TLS read or write which wanted the socket again was not seen as one and dropped the connection with an unrelated error: the C library's errno was set where the socket error is read
! Fix: a client of a connect back (-R) service stayed in accept() for the connection another client of the same service took, until the next one came, past its time out and through a configuration reload; the connect back socket is non-blocking now, and an accept() with nothing to take does not count as one of the client's tries
! Fix: ftppr: the answer of a server which logs in on USER alone (230, as anonymous FTP often does) or refuses the login was read but never handed to the client, which was left waiting for the answer to its PASS until the time out (#1284)
! Fix: plugins: StringsPlugin, cutting a string table line at its end, wrote NULs past the line, into what the buffer kept of longer lines read before or past its end; FilePlugin passed the TLS state of the connection where the client's parameters were expected, so sending a string table over a TLS connection read a TLS state as a clientparam
\+ -B (for TCP services) splits the TLS ClientHello passed through tlspr in the middle of the server name (SNI), so DPI systems which do not reassemble it do not see the host name; TCP_NODELAY, set by default, must not be turned off, or the kernel may join the segments again; -s keeps the same effect where -s is not splice (#1283)
\+ 3proxy --help (and the usage message of a bad invocation) lists what the build was made with: TLS and its backend, RADIUS, PCRE, IPv6, UNIX sockets, the built-in HTTP server, transparency, ODBC and the optional proxy services
\+ An outgoing connection bound to an external address is bound with IP_BIND_ADDRESS_NO_PORT on Linux 4.2 and later: the port is chosen by connect() for the pair with the destination, so ports in use towards other destinations or closing in TIME_WAIT do not run the ephemeral range out; bind() no longer failed with result 12 or searched long for a port under many connections

    3proxy-1.0.3-x64.zip             - Win64 version
    3proxy-1.0.3-x86.zip             - Win32 version
    3proxy-1.0.3-arm64.zip           - Windows for ARM64 (ARMv8) version
    3proxy-1.0.3-lite.zip            - Win32 binaries for older Windo
